steps.title: Sicilian food
steps.body: Nero d'Avola's juicy fruit and fresh acidity suit tomato-based pasta, pizza, grilled sausages and lamb. In Sicily, it goes with pasta alla Norma, made with aubergine, tomato and ricotta salata. Its soft tannins work with tuna or swordfish steaks too.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 15 to 17 degrees. Most Nero d'Avola is best within three to five years, when fruit is bright. Oaked, concentrated versions from top sites age 10 years or more. Cerasuolo di Vittoria can be served slightly cooler.

steps.prompt: Why can Nero d'Avola work with tuna or swordfish?
options: Its soft tannins don't clash with meaty fish
steps.explanation: Soft tannins won't make firm fish taste metallic.

steps.body: Try a lightly chilled Cerasuolo di Vittoria in summer. Its cherry fruit and freshness work like a light red or a serious rosé.

steps.explanation: Sorbet would make the wine taste sour.

points: Nero d'Avola suits tomato pasta, pizza and meaty fish
